A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BrightDreamer. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across the substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation examples, baseline comparisons, component ablations, generation latency, and rendering speed, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds refinement examples, LGM/GRM comparisons, and human-preference percentages.

M1.justification: v2 adds optional post-generation optimization using ISM loss for several hundred iterations (Section 4.3.2). This extends the generation procedure, while the core TSD network, triplane generators, Gaussian decoder, and SDS objective remain.

E1.justification: Vehicle and daily-life evaluation coverage remains, but v1's dedicated animal-and-accessory generation comparison (Figure 9) disappears. v2 still explicitly includes animal descriptions in training, so this is reduced reported evaluation coverage, not established removal of animals from training.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated LGM and GRM comparisons (Figure 9), while removing DreamFusion and ProlificDreamer results previously shown in v1 Figures 7–9. DreamGaussian, GSGEN, LucidDreamer, and Instant3D remain evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v2 introduces human-preference evaluation and a several-hundred-iteration refinement setting, labeled five minutes in Figure 7. It also describes training on one mixed prompt set for about two days, replacing v1's domain-specific 36/60/30-hour descriptions. These are revised reported settings; the PDFs do not establish controlled reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds before-and-after refinement examples testing improvement in detail, but removes the additional ablation cases in v1 Appendix C/Figure 11. The main component ablations remain. The banana generalization examples already appeared in v1's appendix and are redisplayed rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new human-preference percentages are point results without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds preference results of 55.4% for BrightDreamer, 37.3% for Instant3D, and 7.2% for LucidDreamer (Table 2), plus refinement and LGM/GRM qualitative results. Several earlier comparison entries disappear. Table 1's speed values and appendix Figures 12–51 remain unchanged; refinement results use a different procedure, not the original inference setting.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 revises the noisy-input definition from z_t = x + epsilon in v1 to noisy latents encoded from x in v2. This is a localized mathematical-description change. The attention equations are merely consolidated, and no new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the central claims: a first generalizable text-to-Gaussian framework, 77 ms generation, the TSD/TTG design, and strong semantic understanding. Replacing single-stage terminology with feed-forward does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the deterministic single-output limitation with discussion of low spatial resolution and complementary strengths of LGM/GRM. It drops v1's qualification about unequal 64-by-64 supervision, attributes reconstruction-method limitations to scarce 3D data, and gives the retained banana examples a stronger interpretation as evidence of learning text-to-3D distribution mappings.

D1.justification: v1's dataset construction, sources, prompt counts, vocabulary counts, and animal template are omitted from v2, without relocation to its appendix. v2 also removes the explicit 512-by-512 rendering setting and upper-sphere camera restriction. It newly discloses approximately 500M parameters and revises training-time information, but substantially reduces data reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands coverage of SDS variants and image-based reconstruction methods, including LRM, LGM, GRM, and MeshLRM. The standalone 3D Generative Model discussion and several associated references disappear, while positioning increasingly emphasizes avoiding dependence on scarce 3D training data.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative changes from domain-based comparisons to method-family comparisons, refinement, and quantitative evaluation subsections. Related work and appendices are reorganized, the dataset subsection disappears, and terminology and prose are edited throughout.

P2.justification: The manuscript adopts a two-column layout, redraws Figure 1, revises Figure 2's annotations, and substantially restructures the comparison figures. Table 2 is added and existing banana examples receive a main-text display. Appendix Figures 12–51 retain their image content despite repagination.

improvement.justification: v2 adds relevant contemporary comparisons and useful refinement demonstrations, but loses dataset documentation, animal comparisons, and supplementary ablation evidence. Its new preference study omits participant and trial counts, while describing five baseline models although Table 2 lists three methods. These gains and losses leave the net quality change uncertain, particularly because the quantitative addition cannot be assessed reliably from its reported protocol.
